what: W.W. Grainger distributes maintenance, repair and operating supplies: the gloves, fasteners, motors, safety gear and tools that factories, hospitals and public bodies buy repeatedly. It serves large customers through a sales force and smaller ones through the Zoro and MonotaRO websites.
customers: Manufacturers, government agencies, hospitals, schools and contractors in North America and Japan.
money: large customers served by sales representatives and on-site inventory systems
Zoro in the US and MonotaRO in Japan, sold online without a sales force
moat: Next-day availability of hundreds of thousands of items, plus inventory management systems installed inside customer plants.
risks: Demand follows industrial production and construction
Amazon Business competes directly on price and delivery
Tariffs raise the cost of imported goods
Growth is modest at about 5% a year
opportunities: Return on invested capital near 28% is exceptional for a distributor
The online businesses grow faster and need less capital
Customers keep consolidating purchases with fewer, larger suppliers
watch: Daily sales growth and gross margin, which shows whether price increases stick.
